subject: Post-demo: Token economics & continuous batching — FintechX next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoood-inference.com>
To: Sara Li <sara@fintechx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Token economics & continuous batching — FintechX next steps

Hi Sara — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can get you a target pricing proposal:

- Goal: pilot a production inference integration (customer messages -> summarization + classification + short completions) by late Oct.
- Volume signals you shared: 300k monthly active users (MAU) with 2–4 requests/day/user as a baseline; you mentioned a 2–3x burst during promotions.
- Desired unit-econ target: you asked for a ballpark $/1M tokens figure to model into the monthly budget.
- Batching/Concurrency: you called out an expectation of continuous batching (steady stream with steady-state concurrency) vs big batch jobs — want to confirm average request length and % streaming responses so we can size KV cache and batching windows.

What we need from your side to firm up a target price and pilot plan:
1) A 7-day anonymized sample of request logs (timestamps, request token estimates, response token estimates).
2) Expected budget range for pilot (monthly committed spend).
3) Any hard SLAs (p50/p95 latencies) or max concurrency requirements for peak traffic.

Initial assumptions we'll run with (please confirm or correct):
- Average tokens/request: 450 (input + output)
- Steady-state concurrent requests: 60–120 (with short spikes to 350 during promos)
- Continuous batching expected to reduce per-token compute by ~20% vs naive single-request serving in our early estimates

If the above aligns, I'll loop in Marcus (solutions) and Monica (AE) to produce a priced pilot proposal and a mutual action plan (MAP). Attached: redwood-batching-hypotheses.pdf (high-level assumptions).

Next steps: please share the 7-day sample and an initial monthly budget band (e.g., $8k–$25k). We'll return a target $/1M tokens and an estimated pilot cost and slot reservation.

Thanks,
Irene

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoood-inference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoood-inference.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Token economics & continuous batching — FintechX next steps

Looping in with some engineering-level clarifications so the pilot proposal matches production behavior. Quoting Sara below for context:

> - Avg requests/user/day: 3
> - Tokens: Ops estimates ~380 tokens/request on average today but that excludes longer summarization flows (those can be 1k+ tokens occasionally).
> - Concurrency: steady-state concurrency around 45–85; peak promotional windows have hit 420 for short windows historically.

My notes / asks:
- Please confirm request length distribution: percentage of requests < 200 tokens, 200–800, >800. Continuous batching gains depend heavily on the fraction of short completions vs long streaming responses.
- Are long summarizations returned as streaming token-by-token responses, or as a single completion? Streaming has different KV cache behavior and slightly higher per-request overhead; batching windows are shorter.
- What's the acceptable p95 latency for the classification path (short requests)? If sub-300ms p95 is required, we size capacity differently vs a 500–800ms target.

Preliminary pilot config (internal estimate):
- Model family: rwi-llama-compat (8-bit quant)
- Batch window target: 25–40ms (continuous flow) with adaptive batching for short responses
- Expected token-cost lift from continuous batching: 18–25% (depends on short-request fraction)
- Concurrency sizing for pilot slot: reserve 1.2x steady-state (80–120) with capacity for 1h/day of promoted burst up to 420 if we enable burst pool + fallback to cheaper variants.

I'll draft a short MAP and a cost model that outputs the expected $/1M tokens under multiple request mixes. Will attach the model to the next email.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwoood-inference.com

Thanks for the details, Sara — appreciate the estimate and the willingness to pilot. Quick synthesis and an initial target for budgeting so your finance team can model this today:

Summary of confirmed signals:
- MAU: ~310k, avg requests/user/day: 3 -> ~2.79M requests/month baseline
- Token mix: bulk ~380 tokens/request, ~15% requests are long summarizations (avg ~1,200 tokens)
- Concurrency: steady-state 45–85; peaks up to ~420 (short windows)
- Pilot budget: FintechX indicated $10k–$18k/mo provisional

Initial pilot economics (conservative):
- Baseline compute-only token cost (no batching): $22 / 1M tokens
- Projected compute-only token cost with continuous batching (per our pilot config): $17.6 / 1M tokens (~20% lift)
- With caching + request-level optimizations (expected after 2–3 weeks of tuning): target $/1M tokens ~ $15–16

Given your stated budget band, a safe pilot proposal: commit $12k/mo for a 6-week pilot targeting 1.2M requests (sampled traffic) with the goal to demonstrate 15–20% per-token cost reduction and meet p95 latency targets for short requests.

Agreed next steps (timeline):
1) FintechX: share 7-day sample logs to S3 with an ops contact and a point person from procurement for the PO (Sara / procurement). Target: by Fri, 24 Sep.
2) Redwood: deliver a priced MAP and a slot reservation (pilot start tentative Mon, 12 Oct). Target: by Thu, 24 Sep.
3) Both: sign MAP / PO (DocuSign link below) -> Redwood to kick off pilot onboarding and reserve capacity.
